episodes.189134: An upper impulse contributed to an isolated severe thunderstorm.
episodes.189170: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of April 14, 2024. With an unstable atmosphere, one of these thunderstorms strengthened in Robertson County, producing quarter size hail and causing minor wind damage near Springfield.
episodes.189223: During the early evening hours of April 18th, a decaying line of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts across a swath from Knox to Sullivan Counties and eastward as far as Bartholomew County near Columbus.  The damage was most intense in the Knox County area where numerous trees were downed.
episodes.189224: A decaying line of thunderstorms preceding a cold front entered northwestern Alabama early on April 19. One storm within the line briefly intensified in the Haleyville area of Winston County, producing small hail and bringing down several trees and power lines. Later that afternoon, a cluster of storms across northeastern Central Alabama produced a couple instances of small hail, including in Etowah County, where hail up to penny size was observed.
episodes.189719: Severe thunderstorms brought damaging winds and large hail to central and north Arkansas.
episodes.189787: A strong upper trough was present across the Great Lakes region. Combined with this feature was a stalled frontal boundary across western North Carolina and a weak surface low along the South Carolina border. Isolated to scattered storms developed along and east of the US-1 corridor during the afternoon and early evening, with one storm cell becoming severe across Scotland County.
episodes.189835: At the surface, a cold front swept from the western Great Lakes region to central Lake Erie and about halfway eastward through OH during the early to mid-morning hours of the 19th. Ahead of the front, isolated to scattered multicell rain showers and thunderstorms persisted generally northeastward over Lake Erie and produced isolated gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the Ohio shore amidst weak MUCAPE, weak to moderate DCAPE, and moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.189853: A slow moving frontal system aided the development of supercell thunderstorms by mid-afternoon, which eventually grew upscale into a line segment as they progressed across central and southeastern Illinois during the evening. A total of four tornadoes occurred across Logan and Macon counties in central Illinois. One injury occurred in Logan County when a semi-truck was blown over by one of the tornadoes. In addition to the tornadoes, scattered wind damage also occurred.
episodes.190647: A warm front lifted northward through the Quad State region during the morning hours. Dew points near 70 made their way into Southern Illinois, allowing MUCAPE to surge to  1500-2000 J/kg with the higher values in the southwest. 0-3 km SRH peaked around 300 m2/s2 in the evening along I-64 with effective bulk shear of 40-50 kts. Lapse rates were 6-7 C/km. Cells formed in the afternoon, moving northeastward, with a particularly prolific hail producer in Johnson County. The frontal passage moved through during the evening. Wind damage reports in Southern Illinois were primarily on the front moving eastward through Wayne and Franklin Counties. With numerous wind reports and several tornadoes closer to St. Louis, this line weakened on entry to the Quad State, though showed very robust wind speeds a few thousand feet up that just didn't quite mix to the surface. A bit of a break in the frontal storm line showed up in SW Illinois, perhaps a result of a less favorable environment following the afternoon storms in that area.
episodes.190648: A warm front lifted northward through the Quad State region during the morning hours though the late push only allowed dew points to reach the mid 60s in SW Indiana. MUCAPE rose to 1500 J/kg with the higher values in the far SW corner. 0-3 km SRH peaked around 200 m2/s2 in the evening along I-64 with effective bulk shear of 30-40 kts. Lapse rates were 6-7 C/km. Afternoon cells moving northeastward didn't quite reach SW Indiana. The frontal passage moved through during the evening, producing sporadic hail and wind damage reports.
episodes.190649: A warm front lifted northward through the Quad State region during the morning hours. Dew points in the lower 70s made their way into Southeast Missouri, allowing MUCAPE to surge to 2000-2500 J/kg. SRH peaked around 150 m2/s2 in the evening with effective bulk shear around 40 kts. Lapse rates were 6-7 C/km. Cells formed in the afternoon, moving northeastward. The frontal passage moved through late evening. Wind damage reports in SEMO were concentrated on the path of a more north-south oriented portion of the line that showed rotation aloft. A funnel cloud observation was made northwest of Advance with that feature.
episodes.190693: During the afternoon and evening of April 18, 2024, discrete supercell thunderstorms developed along a cold front moving through the bi-state area. These storms were initially capable of producing large hail and damaging wind gusts, but became tornadic as additional thunderstorms formed along the front. Due to the additional thunderstorms, storms congealed into a QLCS that impacted the St. Louis metro area. The QLCS was responsible for a tornado and straight line wind damage in this area. Fortunately, no injuries or fatalities were reported with these thunderstorms.
episodes.190706: During the afternoon and evening of April 18, 2024, discrete supercell thunderstorms developed along a cold front moving through the bi-state area. These storms were initially mainly capable of producing large hail and damaging wind gusts, but become tornadic as additional thunderstorms formed along the front. Due to the additional thunderstorms storms congealed into a QLCS that impacted portions of southwestern Illinois. The QLCS was responsible for several tornadoes and instances of straight line wind damage in this part of the area. Fortunately, no injuries or fatalities were reported with these thunderstorms.
episodes.190766: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced large hail and damaging winds across portions of San Saba County.
episodes.190775: A line of thunderstorms developed during the predawn hours in northwest Alabama. The thunderstorms formed ahead of a southeast moving cold front.  One of the thunderstorms became severe and produced large hail in Franklin County.
episodes.190979: Isolated thunderstorms developed across upstate South Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced isolated large hail and locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.191090: Under a surface-induced perturbation and associated mid to upper-level through...an unsettled workweek was observed for most of the region. Above normal precipitable water (PWAT) values was observed, with available moisture reaching the mid to upper levels. All of this caused the potential for isolated to scattered thunderstorms to increase. Although PWAT values decreased on Wednesday, fairly unstable conditions, diurnal and local effects promoted continued convective development for the second half of the workweek under ENE winds. This weather pattern lead to quick river rises and water surges with flooding, flash flooding, and landslides.
episodes.191094: A cold front brought a line of thunderstorms through southern Indiana. This resulted in a few trees falling down in Dubois, Perry, and Harrison Counties. There was also a tree and power line that caught fire in Dubois County.
episodes.191170: A cold front brought a line of thunderstorms through north central Kentucky. This resulted in a couple of tees down in Meade and Jefferson Counties. The tree in Jefferson County fell and caused damage to a house in St. Matthews.

events.narrative: Public reported ping pong ball size hail.
Penny size hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm near Coopertown.
Quarter size hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm near Springfield.
Severe thunderstorm winds caused a tree to fall on a house along Shelton Street in Springfield. Minor to moderate damage was reported. Damages are a rough estimate.

The tornado touched down about three mile west-southwest of Latham where it snapped off around 10 trees. The tornado was eventually sighted by a spotter about a half mile southwest of Latham, damaging some trees by a home and scouring the ground in the field as it headed toward Latham. The damage in Latham was mainly to trees, with one business having its roof blown off. The tornado dissipated on the east side of Latham at Highway 121. A semi truck was overturned on Route 121, resulting in minor injuries to the driver.
Three power poles were leaning near the intersection of Route 121 and 1842nd Avenue.

The Marion County Sheriff's Office reported a tree down on St. Peter Road at I-57 and a tree on State Route 61 Extension at Lincoln Road. There were other reports of trees uprooted or snapped and a roof blown off. Locations in the path of the storm were Centralia, Salem, Junction City, Sandoval, Odin, Kell, Alma, and Kinmundy.

The tornado touched down just east of the intersection of 2300th Avenue and 200th Street, about 1.5 miles south-southeast of Latham in Logan County, where it produced damage to the roof of an outbuilding. The tornado continued east, crossing into Macon County at the intersection of 2400th Avenue and Heman Street, about two miles southeast of Latham. The tornado eventually dissipated 0.9 miles west of Heman. Softwood and hardwood trees were uprooted along 2400th Avenue, which is the county line between Logan and Macon counties.
Softwood tree limbs were broken off.

The tornado began in Logan County, about 1.5 miles south-southeast of Latham. It progressed east into Macon County, entering the county at the intersection of 2400th Avenue and Heman Street, about 1.75 miles south-southwest of Heman. The tornado uprooted softwood and hardwood trees along 2400th Avenue, which is the county line between Logan and Macon counties. As the tornado progressed east along Heman Street it produced extensive damage to several outbuildings, including knocking down several walls and throwing debris for a mile downstream. The tornado snapped some trees and damaged an outbuilding on 500E Road before dissipating a few hundred yards east of there.
Emergency Managers reported Rio Cibuco out of its banks and flooding a bridge (PR-620) near a local church in Sector Fatima, Vega Alta.

The tornado began about one mile west of Warrensburg along North Kenney Road. It was photographed by the fire chief from Warrensburg as it approached town. The tornado produced roof damage to several homes and damaged numerous trees in Warrensburg. It then traveled along west Illiniwick Road, snapping a couple of large trees before dissipating about a half mile east of north Wyckles Road, which was about 2.5 miles east of Warrensburg.
A semi-truck was blown over on I-72 at Mile Marker 139.

The tornado began two miles north of Forsyth along east Wise Road, damaging numerous trees around a residence. It progressed eastward, damaging grain bins and six power poles just east of Highway 51 along and north of Wise Road. The tornado continued east along east Wise Road and east Emery Road as it progressed towards Argenta. A semi-truck was blown over on Emery Road near Route 51. Debris was strewn all along the path into the adjacent fields. The tornado eventually dissipated about one mile west of Argenta.
Numerous power lines were blown down.
A line of storms moving eastward produced half-dollar size hail in Woodlawn.
Power poles were tilted over on Route 48 between Oreana and Argenta.
A small grain bin was destroyed and blown across the street.
The west-facing side of a farm outbuilding collapsed due to strong wind gusts.
A semi-truck was blown over on Interstate 72 at mile marker 150.
A large tree was blown over.
A large tree was snapped and several other tree branches were blown down.
Four power poles and multiple trees were blown down. A garage roof was damaged.
Thunderstorm winds blew a tree down onto IL-37 near Gun Creek.
A spotter measured a 58 mph wind gust 1 mile north of mile marker 100 on I-64.
Thunderstorm winds from a storm line moving eastward caused a large tree to fall onto a trailer home on Le Roy St in Fairfield.
Due to downburst winds, a couple of power poles snapped and a metal roof was blown off of a large building along US 45 south of County Road 620 N.
Several large trees were blown down.

At least one funnel cloud was spotted west of Advance associated with the storm approaching from the northwest.

Thunderstorm winds blew down multiple large tree limbs of 4-5 inch diameter.
Multiple tree limbs and branches downed by thunderstorm wind gusts along State Road 54 near Eastern Greene Middle School.
